name: Scaredman Recreation Site
note: BLM (Roseburg District) recreation site along Canton Creek in the North Umpqua corridor; 10 minimally-developed sites with tables/fire rings, vault toilet, no hookups (potable water currently off). Reservation-only on recreation.gov (no FCFS, book 5+ days ahead). Canton Creek Rd has grades and curves—challenging for large rigs but a drive-in gravel/paved road. --Claude

name: Buckhorn Campground
note: Small rustic Wallowa-Whitman NF campground (~5 sites, ~5,260 ft) on the Zumwalt Prairie rim near Buckhorn Overlook; open ponderosa/grassland. Reached by ~40 mi of gravel Zumwalt/Forest Rd 46, graded and passable by passenger vehicles when dry (not maintained off-season). Vault toilet, no water, FCFS, June–Sept. --Claude

name: Peninsula Campground (Olallie Lake)
note: USFS Mt. Hood NF (Clackamas River RD) campground on a peninsula in Olallie Lake, ~4,940 ft, in the Olallie Lake Scenic Area. 30+ sites, vault toilets, no potable water; posted max RV/trailer 24 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits the largest sites. First-come, first-served (cash/check drop box); accessed by ~6 mi pavement then ~3 mi gravel off FR 4690 -- rough washboard road, high-clearance helpful but drive-in and passable by a normal vehicle driven slowly. Reopened 2026 after fire recovery (limited shade). --Claude

name: Topsy Campground
note: BLM (Lakeview District) camp on the upper Klamath River (formerly the shore of J.C. Boyle Reservoir, drained after the 2024 Klamath dam removals) ~1.5 mi off Hwy 66 via gravel Topsy Rd. 13 sites, picnic tables/fire rings, drinking water, vault toilets, RV dump station and boat ramp, no hookups; first-come, first-served, open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Odessa Campground
note: Small USFS Fremont-Winema NF camp on Odessa Creek at the west edge of Upper Klamath Lake, off Hwy 140 via FR 3639 (~22 mi W of Klamath Falls). 6 sites (listed to 35 ft but rough access road and tight spacing favor shorter rigs; a 23-ft rig fits), picnic tables/fire rings, one vault toilet, no potable water, small-boat ramp; first-come, first-served, open ~mid-May to mid-Dec. --Claude

name: Spool Cart Campground
note: USFS Wallowa-Whitman NF (La Grande RD) camp on the banks of the Grande Ronde River, ~5 mi south of Hwy 244 on FR 51. 12 tent/trailer sites (spurs ~33-45 ft, incl 3 double/group), paved roads, accessible vault toilets, no potable water; first-come, first-served via self-pay. --Claude

name: Drews Creek Campground
note: Small FCFS Fremont-Winema NF forest camp on Drews Creek off Dog Lake Rd, ~35 min SW of Lakeview; about 5 drive-in sites (space for 4-5 small RVs plus tents), picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilets, no potable water. Gravel access. --Claude

name: Holbrook Reservoir Campground
note: FCFS Fremont-Winema NF campground on Holbrook Reservoir (Lofton Recreation Area, Bly RD), ~35 min SE of Bly; 4 designated sites plus ~8 dispersed sites, picnic tables/fire rings, 2 vault toilets, boat ramp and dock (electric motors only), no potable water. Drive-in off FS 3715/3817. --Claude

name: Lee Thomas Campground
note: FCFS Fremont-Winema NF campground on the Wild & Scenic North Fork Sprague River, SW of Paisley; 7 drive-in sites for tents/RVs/trailers, picnic tables/fire grates, vault toilet, potable water, open ~May 15-Oct 15. Area burned in the 2021 Bootleg Fire but the campground reopened. --Claude

name: Mud Creek Campground
note: Small FCFS Fremont-Winema NF forest camp (Lakeview RD, E side of the Warner Mtns) ~35 min NE of Lakeview; 7 spacious back-in drive-in sites among ponderosa/lodgepole/aspen, picnic tables/fire grates, vault toilet, hand-pump potable water, gravel FS 3615 access, open ~May 15-Oct 15. --Claude

name: Twin Springs Campground
note: Small FCFS Fremont-Winema NF forest camp (Lakeview RD, Warner Mtns) at ~6,480 ft SE of Lakeview; 3 drive-in sites among ponderosa/white fir/aspen by the spring, picnic tables/fire grates, vault toilet, no potable water. Gravel FS-road access. --Claude

name: Willow Creek Campground
note: Small FCFS Fremont-Winema NF forest camp (Lakeview RD, Warner Mtns) at ~6,073 ft along Willow Creek; 8 drive-in sites among ponderosa/aspen, picnic tables/fire grates, vault toilet, no potable water, open ~May 15-Oct 15. Gravel FS-road access. --Claude

name: Trout Creek Campground
note: BLM Prineville District campground on the Lower Deschutes Wild & Scenic River near Gateway/Madras. 21 individual sites plus 3 group-use sites, no hookups, vault toilets, no potable water; parking spurs 24-100 ft with some pull-throughs (fits a 23-ft rig). First-come, first-served (pay kiosk/fee box); open year-round. Access is gravel with a 14-ft-high tunnel near the entrance (height, not length, limit). --Claude

name: Wildwood Campground
note: Ochoco National Forest, small rustic camp in ponderosa pine/larch/fir east of the Ochoco Divide RNA, reached via FS Rd 2630/2210 off Hwy 26. 5 sites, 24 ft max RV, pit toilets, no water or trash (pack in/out). First-come, first-served, open ~June–Sept. --Claude

name: Black Canyon Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF, on the Middle Fork Willamette River ~1 mi from Lookout Point Lake, 8 mi west of Oakridge off Hwy 58. 75 sites in mature Douglas-fir/cedar forest, RVs to ~44 ft; drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. 19 sites reservable via recreation.gov, remainder first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Islet Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (Middle Fork RD) campground at the north end of Waldo Lake, just S of North Waldo. 55 sites (31 reservable, rest FCFS), no hookups, vault toilets; RVs to 43 ft. Sandy beaches, boat launch (electric motors only). Open ~June-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Sand Prairie Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (Middle Fork RD) campground on the Middle Fork Willamette River above Hills Creek Reservoir, off FR 21. 21 individual drive-in sites (FCFS unless a site carries a 'Reserved' placard), no potable water, no hookups, vault toilets. River reached by a short path; S trailhead of the Middle Fork Willamette Trail. --Claude

name: Shadow Bay Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (Middle Fork RD) campground on the SE shore of Waldo Lake. 92 sites (19 reservable, rest FCFS), no hookups, vault toilets; max trailer length 32 ft per Willamette NF. Boat launch (electric motors only), swimming, kayaking. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Nottingham Campground
note: USFS Mt. Hood NF campground on the East Fork Hood River right off Hwy 35. 21-23 sites, no hookups, vault toilets, no potable water; max vehicle length ~32 ft. Reservable on recreation.gov (some sites FCFS), open ~Memorial Day-September. --Claude

name: Sugar Creek Campground
note: USFS Ochoco NF (Paulina RD) campground straddling Sugar Creek in a ponderosa pine flat off a paved FS road ~13 mi NE of Paulina. Sites vary in size; many accommodate moderate-sized RVs, no hookups, no potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Hart Mountain Hot Springs Campground
note: Primitive campground in Hart Mountain National Antelope Refuge (USFWS), ~4 mi south of refuge HQ near the Antelope hot springs. ~25-30 spread-out sites for tents and trailers up to 24 ft, vault toilets, fire rings, no water/hookups. No reservations, 14-day limit, open year-round; reached on maintained gravel roads (Hart Mountain/Hot Springs Rd) passable by most vehicles. --Claude

name: Oregon Sunstone Public Collection Area
note: BLM Lakeview District free public rockhounding area (dispersed camping, no designated sites) in the Rabbit Basin ~20+ mi N of Plush. Facilities are a pit toilet, picnic tables and a shade structure; camp anywhere in the collection area. Main area reached on graded gravel (Hogback Rd/CR 3-10 then BLM roads); high-clearance recommended for the rough interior 2-tracks to prime digging spots. First-come, first-served, no hookups/water. --Claude

name: Butler Bar Campground
note: Small Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Powers RD) campground on the Wild & Scenic Elk River, ~22 mi up FR 5325 from Hwy 101. 7 drive-in sites, picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilet, no potable water. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit; maintained forest-road access. --Claude

name: Edson Creek Campground
note: BLM Coos Bay District (Myrtlewood Field Office) campground ~4 mi up Sixes River Rd from Hwy 101, on Edson Creek near the Sixes River. 27 individual sites plus 5 group sites; no hookups, potable water at kiosk, boat ramp/day-use across the road. Half the main loop is FCFS, half reservable online; group sites reservation-only. Open ~Memorial Day to Sept 30. --Claude

name: Laird Lake Campground
note: Tiny primitive Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Powers RD) campground at little Laird Lake near the Elk River headwaters, ~28 mi up FR 5325 (pavement ends; last stretch is a rough, steep, rocky forest road — good ground clearance advised, not 4WD-required). 4 drive-in sites, picnic tables/fire pits, vault toilet, no water. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit; best for smaller rigs. --Claude

name: Sunshine Bar Campground
note: Small primitive Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Powers RD) campground on the Wild & Scenic Elk River, ~19 mi up FR 5325 from Hwy 101 (first of the Elk River FS camps coming from the coast). 6 drive-in sites, picnic tables/fire pits, vault toilet, no potable water. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Antelope Flat Reservoir Campground
note: Ochoco NF campground at ~5,000 ft on a single loop near 170-acre Antelope Flat Reservoir, ~40 mi SE of Prineville via Hwy 380/FR 17. 23 sites incl pull-through RV spaces, no hookups, hand-pump potable water, vault toilet; boat ramp and day-use at the water's edge. First-come, first-served, mid-May to mid-Oct. Sites are a short walk back from the water. --Claude

name: Crescent Campground
note: Small rustic Malheur NF (Prairie City RD) campground at ~5,180 ft on the Little (Baby) John Day River, ~17 mi from Prairie City via CR 62. 4 drive-in sites, picnic tables/fire rings, pit toilet, no potable water; a base for the Strawberry Mountain Wilderness. First-come, first-served, ~May-Oct, 14-day limit. Older/rustic facilities. --Claude

name: Jackman Park Campground
note: 6-site BLM (Burns District) campground in an aspen grove at ~7,650 ft on the Steens Mountain Loop Road; vault/universal-access restroom, no potable water; open mid-June-Oct, 14-day limit. Drive-in on the maintained Steens Loop Road. First-come, first-served, $16/night. --Claude

name: Chimney Rock Segment Campgrounds
note: BLM Prineville District string of ~9 small first-come, first-served campgrounds along the Lower Crooked Wild & Scenic River on Hwy 27 south of Prineville (Castle Rock, Stillwater, Lone Pine, Palisades, Chimney Rock, Cobble Rock, Post Pile, Poison Butte, Big Bend); ~97 total sites. Pinned to the main Chimney Rock Campground (16 sites, RVs to 32 ft, vault toilets, potable water, grey-water sumps). Open year-round, no reservations. --Claude

name: Deep Creek Campground
note: Ochoco National Forest campground among large ponderosa pine on the North Fork Crooked River at the mouth of Deep Creek; paved access most of the way. 15 well-spaced sites good for RVs and tents, vault/pit toilets, no potable water. 14-day limit; FCFS (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Ochoco Divide Campground
note: Ochoco National Forest campground in ponderosa pine at the top of Ochoco Divide (~4,700 ft) just off US-26, ~30 mi east of Prineville. 25 single sites with large pull-throughs (over half fit a 40-ft rig), four vault toilets, no potable water. Individual sites FCFS; group site reservable on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Eagle Forks Campground
note: Wallowa-Whitman NF (Whitman RD) small primitive campground below the Wild & Scenic Eagle Creek / Little Eagle Creek confluence, ~7.75 mi up mostly single-lane gravel FR 7735 from New Bridge. 7 tent/trailer sites, no hookups, seasonal drinking water; scan-and-pay/FCFS. No published max length; small forest sites. --Claude

name: Chickahominy Reservoir
note: BLM Burns District high-desert campground on Chickahominy Reservoir along US-20 ~32 mi W of Burns. 28 gravel-pad sites suitable for RVs, drinking water, vault toilets, fish-cleaning station and boat ramp; all sites first-come, first-served (no reservations). Popular trout fishery. --Claude

name: Elderberry Flat Campground
note: BLM Medford District primitive campground along the West Fork of Evans Creek NW of Rogue River, paved access. 11 paved primitive sites, picnic tables/grills, one pit toilet, no water/hookups; 14-day limit, FCFS. Multiple creek-access points with granite sand bars. In an OHV/trail area. --Claude

name: Clearwater Falls Campground
note: Umpqua NF (Diamond Lake RD) small campground on the Clearwater River near Clearwater Falls off Hwy 138. 9 sites (5 off Hwy 138, 4 upper via FR 4785), no hookups, no potable water; first-come, first-served (June-Oct). Vehicles 25 ft max due to winding approach. --Claude

name: Hemlock Lake Campground
note: Umpqua NF (North Umpqua RD) campground at 28-acre Hemlock Lake reservoir, reached via ~32 mi of Little River Rd (FR 27) from Glide. 1 double + 9 sites that fit RVs/trailers (to ~35 ft) plus 3 tent-only sites; no hookups, no drinking water; open terrain adjacent to the lake, trout fishing. First-come, first-served (June-Oct). --Claude

name: Hemlock Meadows Campground
note: Umpqua NF (Diamond Lake RD) developed campground on 28-acre Hemlock Lake reservoir, ~32 mi up NF Rd 27 (gravel) from Hwy 138. Small (4-5 tent/trailer sites), max vehicle length 35 ft, boat launch at campground edge, no drinking water/trash (pack it out). Pay onsite via rec.gov Scan & Pay app (no advance reservations). --Claude

name: Susan Creek Campground
note: BLM (Roseburg District) campground on the North Umpqua Wild & Scenic River at milepost 28 on Hwy 138, ~29 mi east of Roseburg. 29 sites on one loop, RVs listed 21+ ft, flush toilets and hot showers; 13 sites reservable online (May 15-Sep 15), 16 first-come first-served. --Claude

name: Rufus Landing Recreation Area
note: USACE (John Day project) dispersed camping area: a level gravel flat on the Columbia River (Lake Umatilla) just west of John Day Dam, I-84 exit 109 at Rufus. Accommodates RVs up to ~45 ft, vault toilets, boat/kayak launch, no hookups; first-come first-served, 7-day limit. --Claude
